# P04 — Identity & auth

Depends on: P00, P01, P03
Branch: `phase/04-identity-auth`
Implements: ROLE-USER, ROLE-PARTNER, ROLE-MERCHANT, ROLE-ADMIN · architecture 2.7

## Scope

Phone + OTP as the primary factor, JWT access tokens, refresh-token rotation
backed by Redis, RBAC middleware, rate limiting, and device sessions — for all
four roles.

## Token model

| Token | Lifetime | Storage | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Access (JWT) | 15 min | Client memory, never on disk | Stateless. Carries `sub`, `role`, `session_id`, `exp`, `jti`. Verified by signature only — no Redis read on the hot path. |
| Refresh (opaque, 256-bit random) | 60 days, sliding | Client secure storage (Keystore / Keychain); server stores **only a SHA-256 hash** in Redis | Single-use. Every use rotates it. |

Access tokens are deliberately stateless so that the common request path costs
no Redis round trip. Revocation power lives with the refresh token, and the
short access lifetime bounds the blast radius to 15 minutes.

### Redis keys

```
session:<session_id>              hash   user_id, role, device, created_at, last_seen_at
                                         TTL = refresh lifetime
refresh:<sha256(token)>           string session_id
                                         TTL = refresh lifetime, single-use
refresh_family:<session_id>       set    every hash ever issued for this session
otp:<phone>                       string hashed OTP, TTL = otp.ttl
otp_attempts:<phone>              string verify counter, TTL = otp.lockout_window
rate:<scope>:<identifier>         string fixed-window counter
```

TTLs mean expiry is automatic — no sweeper job, and a logged-out session cannot
linger.

## Auto-login (silent re-authentication)

**Requirement: if the user is logged out but holds a valid refresh token, they
are signed back in without seeing the login screen.**

Flow on app start, and on any `401` from an API call:

1. Client reads the refresh token from secure storage. Absent → login screen.
2. Client calls `POST /auth/refresh` with it.
3. Server hashes the token, looks up `refresh:<hash>`.
   - **Hit** → issue a new access token *and* a new refresh token, delete the
     old hash, add the new hash to the family set, extend the session TTL,
     return both. The client replaces the stored token. User lands on Home.
   - **Miss, but hash present in `refresh_family:<session_id>`** → this token
     was already rotated, so it has been replayed. Treat as theft: revoke the
     entire family, delete the session, return `401 token_reuse_detected`. The
     client wipes storage and shows the login screen.
   - **Unknown hash** → `401 invalid_refresh_token`.
4. Concurrency: step 3 runs as an atomic Lua script (GETDEL + family add) so two
   in-flight refreshes from the same device cannot both mint a token or trip the
   reuse alarm spuriously. The client additionally coalesces concurrent refreshes
   into one in-flight request.

The client never decides whether a token is valid or when to refresh — it reacts
to `401` and to the `expires_in` the server returns (2.9: no business rule in the
app).

```

P04.T02  Ports: OTPStore, SessionStore, RefreshTokenStore, TokenSigner, RateLimiter, SMSSender
P04.T03  Use case: RequestOTP — generation, hashing, TTL, resend cooldown
P04.T04  Use case: VerifyOTP — attempt cap, lockout, session + token pair issue
P04.T05  Use case: RefreshSession — rotation, reuse detection, atomic swap
P04.T06  Use case: Logout and LogoutAllDevices — family revocation
P04.T07  Infrastructure: Redis stores (Lua rotation script), JWT signer, SMS adapter
P04.T08  Transport: /auth endpoints, RBAC middleware, rate-limit middleware, OpenAPI
P04.T09  IdentityContract + external/ services for consuming modules
P04.T10  Tests: unit, contract, integration against real Redis, concurrency and reuse cases
P04.T11  Docs: technical + user; ADR 0005 update if the model changes
P04.T12  Coverage verification, PR, merge
```

## Endpoints

| Method | Path | Role | Purpose |
|---|---|---|---|
| POST | `/auth/otp/request` | public, rate-limited | Send an OTP to a phone number |
| POST | `/auth/otp/verify` | public, rate-limited | Verify OTP, create session, return token pair |
| POST | `/auth/refresh` | public, rate-limited | Rotate refresh token, return a new pair |
| POST | `/auth/logout` | any authenticated | Revoke the current session |
| POST | `/auth/logout-all` | any authenticated | Revoke every session for the user |
| GET | `/auth/sessions` | any authenticated | List active devices |

Every endpoint declares its required role explicitly; there are no implicit
public endpoints (2.7). The role is enforced in middleware **and** re-checked in
the use case.

## Rate limits (config keys, per Appendix B resolution order)

| Key | Default | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `auth.otp_request_per_hour` | 5 | Per phone number |
| `auth.otp_verify_attempts` | 5 | Before lockout |
| `auth.otp_lockout_window` | 900 s | Lockout duration |
| `auth.otp_ttl` | 300 s | OTP validity |
| `auth.access_token_ttl` | 900 s | Access token lifetime |
| `auth.refresh_token_ttl` | 5184000 s | Refresh token lifetime (60 days) |
| `auth.max_sessions_per_user` | 5 | Oldest session evicted beyond this |

## Acceptance

- A user who has never signed in can request an OTP, verify it and receive an access + refresh pair.
- Restarting the app with a valid refresh token lands on Home without a login screen.
- An expired access token triggers exactly one silent refresh, and the original request is retried.
- A refresh token works exactly once; presenting it a second time revokes the whole session family.
- Two concurrent refreshes from one device yield one rotation, not a false theft alarm.
- Logout invalidates the refresh token immediately; the access token stops working within its 15-minute ceiling.
- OTP brute force is stopped by the attempt cap and the lockout window.
- A partner token cannot call a merchant endpoint, enforced in middleware and re-checked in the use case.
